Mail Drop on the device vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Mail large-file capability covers storefront language. Mail compose behavior and App Store Connect actually separate system Mail Drop from product-page copy:

  • Mail Drop on the device — when a Mail attachment exceeds typical SMTP size limits, Apple Mail uploads the file to iCloud and embeds a download link in the outgoing message instead of attaching the raw file. Recipients download from iCloud; links expire after a set period. System Mail behavior — outside AppLocale scope.
  • iCloud upload and link delivery — Mail Drop relies on the sender's iCloud storage and Apple's Mail infrastructure. Configuring buyer iCloud accounts or Mail transport is user-side setup — AppLocale does not upload attachments for buyers and does not operate Mail servers on their behalf.
  • Mail Drop marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app works with Mail Drop, recommends large-attachment send via iCloud links, or documents honest compatibility with Mail compose overflow flows. Connect text fields — this page.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China storefront. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Mail Drop positioning in the app.

An app that references Mail Drop or large-attachment email workflows in onboarding and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe Mail Drop and iCloud large-file email send on the store page, not whether a buyer's Mail account supports Mail Drop on device.

What Mail Drop actually does — listing honesty

Apple ships Mail Drop as a Mail feature that uploads oversized attachments to iCloud and sends recipients a download link when direct SMTP attachment would fail. Third-party apps may complement this by educating buyers, aligning compose UX with large-file send expectations, or documenting honest compatibility with Mail Drop workflows. AppLocale FAQ

What is Apple Mail Drop?

Mail Drop is a Mail feature that sends large email attachments via iCloud when files exceed typical SMTP attachment size limits. Mail uploads the file to iCloud and sends recipients a download link — typically supporting large files up to about 5 GB class. Marketing that awareness on your en-US page does not auto-fill zh-Hans Connect fields.

Does mentioning Mail Drop auto-translate my China listing?

No. Mail Drop is a system Mail feature on the buyer's device — it does not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback on the product page.

How is Mail Drop different from AirDrop?

Mail Drop sends oversized email attachments via iCloud download links in Mail — 邮件投递, Mail Drop附件, 大型附件邮件. AirDrop sends files wirelessly to nearby Apple devices — 隔空投送, 附近分享. Email attachment overflow and nearby device transfer are separate features. See our AirDrop listing guide only when nearby wireless send is your lead claim.

How is Mail Drop different from NameDrop?

Mail Drop covers large email attachment send via iCloud links. NameDrop covers contact poster and phone-number exchange when devices are brought together. See our NameDrop listing guide only when contact exchange is your lead claim.
